Four households are billed in two groups even though they signed a householding agreement to be billed as one: **HH-0586, HH-0592, HH-0928 and HH-4821.**

Each case follows the same pattern. The CRM (`crm/crm.json`) records a signed householding agreement, a "Householding letter". It says the joint account, the spouse's IRA and the child's individual account "are billed together as one group from the next billing cycle." The portfolio system (`portfolio/household.json`) still has two billing groups as of 15 April 2026. The joint account and the IRA are in group 1, and the child's account is billed alone in group 2. Both groups were last changed before the agreement was signed, so the system was never updated for it.

| Household | Agreement | Signed | Billing groups | Groups last changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0592 (Haddad) | AGR-0592-3 | 2023-10-20 | BG-0592-1 (…0001, …0002), BG-0592-2 (…0003) | 2021-09-01 |
| HH-0586 (Quarshie) | AGR-0586-3 | 2024-06-07 | BG-0586-1 (…0001, …0002), BG-0586-2 (…0003) | 2021-09-01 |

| HH-4821 (Okafor-Lind/Lind) | AGR-4821-3 | 2024-11-18 | BG-4821-1 (…0001, …0002), BG-4821-2 (…0003) | 2021-09-14 |

For these four:
- **Nothing in the files explains the split.** I found no later reversal, exception or correction, and every account is still open at the custodian (`custodian/accounts.csv`). The October 2025 annual review notes say "No changes requested."
- **Why it matters for fees:** the standard schedule (`portfolio/billing.json`) applies its tiered rates to each billing group separately. Billing the child's account apart means the household's combined value isn't used for the lower rates above $1M and $2M. I didn't calculate the dollar overcharge because you didn't ask for it; I can do that from the quarter-end values if you want.

Only these four CRM files mention a householding agreement. Four other households are also billed in two groups, but none of them contradicts an agreement:
- **HH-0478, HH-0517 and HH-0572** have only separate advisory agreements.
- **HH-7350:** the separate advisory agreement AGR-7350-2 says Aiko "has not agreed to household billing", so billing that account alone is correct.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which households are billed in groups that a signed householding agreement contradicts?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households are, "none_found" if none is, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household that is, each as {"household_id": ..., "agreement_id": the householding agreement, "billing_group_ids": the billing groups that hold its accounts apart, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
